question.problem: Given that the random variable $X∼\text{Exp}(4),$ calculate $P(\frac{1}{2}<X<\frac{3}{4}).$ Round your final answer to four decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
An exponential random variable $X$ with rate $\lambda $ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\lambda {e}^{-\lambda x}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that

$$
X∼\text{Exp}(4).
$$

So, $X$ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}4{e}^{-4x}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate $P(\frac{1}{2}<X<\frac{3}{4})$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\frac{1}{2}<X<\frac{3}{4}) & ={\int }_{1/2}^{3/4}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1/2}^{3/4}4{e}^{-4x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{e}^{-4x}{|}_{1/2}^{3/4} \\  & =-{e}^{-3}+{e}^{-2} \\  & ≈0.0855\end{aligned}
$$
